questions_and_answers.question: Where is the fare meter located in a Japanese taxi?
Do you need to tip the taxi driver in Japan?

answers.answer: No, you don't need to tip
Only if the driver helps with luggage

questions_and_answers.question: How do you ask 'How much is it?' to confirm the fare?
What can you say to thank the driver after paying?
Should you be surprised if a taxi driver doesn't respond much?

answers.answer: No, some drivers may not be very sociable and may not say anything until you give them the destination

questions_and_answers.question: What denomination of bills is a good idea to have available?

answers.answer: 500-yen or 1,000-yen bills (when the destination is not very far)

questions_and_answers.question: Why should you have smaller bills available?

answers.answer: Because the driver may not be able to change a large bill
Because tips need to be in small bills

questions_and_answers.question: What does the simple act of paying the fare in Japan involve?

answers.answer: Looking at the meter and paying the fare before you get out

questions_and_answers.question: Does the lesson encourage tipping cab drivers in Japan?

answers.answer: No, since you don't need to tip in Japan

questions_and_answers.question: How would you typically pay attention to the cost of the ride?

answers.answer: Look at the fare meter in the front

articles.text:
3. How to pay the fare

Since every taxi has a fare meter in the front and you don't need to tip, you can simply look at the meter and pay the fare before you get out. If you want to make sure of the fare, you can, of course, ask the following question:

Ikura desu ka?    How much is it?

When you get out, after having paid the fare, you can say:

Doomo (arigatoo).    Thank you

However, don't be surprised if the driver doesn't respond. S/he may not be very sociable. Some drivers may not say anything until you give them the destination when you get in the cab, or even after you give it to them.

It would be a good idea for you to have 500-yen or 1,000-yen bills available when the destination is not very far, as it may happen that the driver is not able to change a large bill.
